decisions_this_run: D-075a: the window is a domain policy, not a request field. No caller can express 'delete everything' or 'delete Bob's rows' because there is no field for it.
D-075b: erasing is its own authority (access-log-retention), distinct from operator-access-report, so the read can be granted widely and the erase narrowly.
D-075c: the purge records itself through the gate before deleting, stamped now - inside the window it prunes - so it cannot erase the record of its own action.
D-075d: retention is off by default and the endpoint 404s when unconfigured, rather than offering a purge with no mandate. A too-short window fails the boot, not the first purge.
D-075e: the boundary is inclusive at its near edge, and one rule drives both the adapter and covers() so they cannot disagree at the oldest surviving row.
run_summary: Run 75 closed the second risk run 74 recorded: the durable operator access log was append-only and unbounded, so one row per granted /ops read accumulated forever, each attributed to a named user. No backlog task existed, so NEX-075 was created first. The design point is that the obvious fix - let an operator delete rows - destroys the property the log exists for, so deletion is bounded from every direction: a validated domain window, a distinct erase authority, a self-recording purge, and off-by-default retention. ADR-017 records the decisions and what was deliberately not done (a scheduled purge). Also fixed the ADR index, which had never listed ADR-016. One correction worth recording: this run first assumed PR #5's body stopped at NEX-073 and wrote that into STATE, the checkpoint and the execution log. The GitHub API showed it already carries NEX-074. All three were corrected before commit, and the correction is left visible rather than silently rewritten. CI on 319a3dd was read at the end of the run: 4/4 completed/success, so NEX-075 is VERIFIED, not merely pushed. PR #5's body was extended with the single NEX-075 section (56934 -> 60453 chars) and issue #2 received comment 7232583113.
